text: Every business exists for one reason. To make money.
Money comes from customers. And customers come from marketing.
Marketing is spending money today, to win customers tomorrow. So every marketing decision comes down to one question. Where should the next dollar go?
And the menu is overwhelming. Conferences. Billboards. Google Ads. Cold email. LinkedIn. S.E.O. And now, answers from A.I. assistants.
Every channel speaks a different language. Badge scans. Impressions. Clicks. Replies. Leads. Rankings. Some pay off in days. Others take months.
So decisions get made by gut feeling, by the loudest voice, or by whatever number is easiest to count. That's the trap.
LinkedIn brings in the cheapest leads. And some of the most expensive customers.
The fix starts from first principles. Translate every channel into one currency, close to money: the cost of a qualified sales lead.
Then ask what the next dollar buys. Because every channel gets more expensive, the more you pour in.
Move money from where the next customer is expensive, to where it is cheap. Small steps. Measure. Repeat. Every week.
That loop is the job of a C.M.O. Repetitive, data heavy, and never finished. A perfect job for agents.
One agent per channel speaks that channel's language. A C.M.O. agent decides where the money goes. And the C.E.O. sets the goal, and how much the agent may move on its own.
Small moves, it makes by itself. Big ones come to you, with the evidence. One click.
Agentic C.M.O. The C.E.O. steers. The agent runs marketing.
